animation: closed -> open, left to right (play backwards to close)
anchor: the LAST 16 rows of a frame (rows 16..31, own_cell_row..) are the piece's own doorway cell; every row above overlaps the cells to the NORTH (doors draw over the wall there). Draw the frame with its top-left at (cell.x*16, cell.y*16 - own_cell_row), region 16x32 (frame_size) at (frame*16, atlas_y).
projection: wall height: 8px face + top strip shifted up 8px, same as the wall tiles; closed slab sits on the seam between the two doorway cells

usage.horizontal doorway (gap in a north/south: paint on the SOUTH cell of each column, the north cell stays floor. width 1: h_single. width N, column i: i==0 h_end_left, i==N-1 h_end_right, else h_middle_left when i < N/2 otherwise h_middle_right.
usage.vertical doorway (gap in an east/west wa: each doorway row gets a *_left piece on the WEST cell and the matching *_right piece on the EAST cell. height 1: v_single. height N, row i: i==0 v_end_top, i==N-1 v_end_bottom, else v_middle_top when i < N/2 otherwise v_middle_bottom.

split: each 16x32 frame is 2 16x16 tiles, the last one on the doorway cell itself, the ones above it on the cells NORTH of it (over the wall).
note: dedicated 5-wide bi-fold door: each side is two 20px panels, the outer hinged on the jamb, the inner folding back with its end on a rail along the seam (rows 15..16 / columns 15..16, under the closed slab). Open: horizontal stacks on rows 4..31 inside the doorway, vertical stacks on the wall face above (rows 8..21) and, cut, on the doorway's last 6 rows; the rail shows between them. Column/row 2 uses the _2 piece names.
